entities.summary: Naryshkin Baroque, also referred to as Moscow Baroque or Muscovite Baroque, is a particular style of Baroque architecture and decoration that was fashionable in Moscow from the late 17th century into the early 18th century. In the late 17th century, the Western European Baroque style of architecture combined with traditional Russian architecture to form this unique style. It is called Muscovite Baroque as it was originally only found within Moscow and the surrounding areas. It is more commonly referred to as Naryshkin Baroque, as the first church designed in this style was built on one of the Naryshkin family's estates.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Naryshkin Baroque style played a significant role in shaping Moscow's architectural identity during the early 18th century, influencing the design of numerous churches and palaces. Its unique blend of Western European and traditional Russian elements helped to establish Moscow as a major cultural center.
